rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child. Beyond the standard monument formula, the two proclamations share a distinctive modern sequence of findings: Tribal sacredness since time immemorial; protection of all identified objects whether or not expressly labeled; threats and inadequacy of existing protections; necessity of an Antiquities Act reservation; and smallest-compatible-area findings. Both then establish a monument covering geographically discrete landscapes and employ Tribal-centered management informed by Indigenous Knowledge. C10 is especially close in its advisory-committee and Tribal commission machinery, while C05 shares much of the Biden-era findings and co-stewardship structure, but C07 is the closest overall combination of language, rationale, and administrative design.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas, the Chuckwalla region has been profoundly sacred to Tribal Nations and Indigenous peoples with ties to the Colorado and Mojave Deserts since time immemorial
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas, the landscapes of the areas to the northeast, northwest, and south of the Grand Canyon have been profoundly sacred to Tribal Nations and Indigenous peoples of the Southwest since time immemorial
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel recital framing a multi-area desert landscape as profoundly sacred to Tribal Nations since time immemorial.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I find that all the objects identified above, and objects of the type identified above within the area described herein, are objects of historic or scientific interest in need of protection ... regardless of whether they are expressly identified
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I find that all the objects identified above are objects of historic or scientific interest in need of protection ... regardless of whether they are expressly identified as objects of historic or scientific interest in the text of this proclamation
shared_material.explanation: Closely shared finding extending protection beyond objects expressly identified in the narrative.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I find that there are threats to the objects identified in this proclamation, and, in the absence of a reservation under the Antiquities Act ... [they] are not adequately protected by applicable law or administrative designations, thus making a national monument designation and reservation necessary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I find that there are threats to the objects identified above, and, in the absence of a reservation under the Antiquities Act, these objects are not adequately protected by the current withdrawal, administrative designations, or otherwise applicable law ... thus a national monument ... is necessary
shared_material.explanation: The same detailed threats–inadequate protection–necessary reservation logic appears in nearly the same operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary shall meaningfully engage with Tribal Nations with cultural or historical affiliation ... including by seeking opportunities for co-stewardship of the monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Conserving lands ... through an abiding partnership between the United States and the region's Tribal Nations
shared_material.explanation: Both use Tribal partnership and Indigenous expertise as a substantive monument-management principle, not merely a generic consultation clause.
